primary_sources.title: On sharp bounds for marginal densities of product measures
primary_sources.authors: Galyna Livshyts; Grigoris Paouris; Peter Pivovarov
primary_sources.used_scope: one-dimensional normalized linear-form density cap sqrt(2) for cap-one product inputs

primary_sources.title: Small Ball Probabilities for Linear Images of High-Dimensional Distributions
primary_sources.used_scope: compatible source for linear-image anti-concentration; not used to add any extra hypothesis

new_result.statement: For disjoint original product banks X,Y,Z, T=X^T M Y+alpha^T X+G(Y)+a(beta^T Z+H(Y))^2 has a continuous C0 density bounded by 8 K_beta/sqrt(|a| ||M||op), where K_beta is the density cap of beta^T Z. LPP gives K_beta<=sqrt(2)/||beta||. For a single original coordinate in the square the constant is 8/sqrt(|a| ||M||op).

partner_result_applied.actual_equation: On Q=2 X^T diag(1,epsilon)Y+lambda W^2, partner gives 2 sqrt(2 pi)/sqrt(epsilon), while new result gives 4 sqrt(2)/sqrt(lambda). At epsilon=1/2, lambda=64: 7.0898154036220635 versus 0.7071067811865476.

unresolved_implication: Derive or replace the zero X-W coupling / nonzero scalar-pivot geometry from s3(A)>=1 while retaining a near-rank-two two-sided cross tail exactly.
next_step: Try an anchored moving-square theorem that keeps a nonzero X-W vector r and spends the component of C transverse to r jointly with the scalar square, rather than deleting the anchor.
